claims.text: The investigated alloy has the nominal composition Ti30Ni30Al20V10Cr10.
Every constituent of Ti30Ni30Al20V10Cr10 lies within the stated 5–35 at% high-entropy-alloy range.
The as-produced Ti30Ni30Al20V10Cr10 alloy is a homogeneous solid solution.
The intervention consists of solution treatment at 1100°C for 1 hour under argon, rapid quenching, and aging near 850°C for about 2 hours.
The two-step treatment will produce a homogeneous distribution of nanoscale precipitates in Ti30Ni30Al20V10Cr10.
The precipitates produced in the Ti-Ni matrix will be coherent intermetallics, such as sigma or Laves phase.
Systematic variation of aging time and temperature can regulate precipitate size and distribution.
Maintaining the precipitates at nanoscale dimensions will avoid over-aging, coarsening, and embrittlement.
The nanoscale precipitates will pin dislocations.
The precipitates will stabilize the high-temperature microstructure by hindering grain-boundary sliding and retarding coarsening.
Precipitation strengthening will increase the alloy's yield strength at 800°C.
The heat-treated alloy will have approximately 20–30% greater yield strength at 800°C than the as-cast alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have improved creep resistance at 800°C relative to the as-cast alloy.
Improved creep resistance will appear as reduced creep-strain accumulation and increased rupture life.
The untreated as-cast condition has lower high-temperature yield strength and an earlier onset of creep strain than the proposed heat-treated condition.
An inert heat-treatment environment will prevent or reduce oxidation.
The proposed intervention is intended for titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloys whose constituent concentrations are each 5–35 at%.
The proposed operating boundary extends to service temperatures of approximately 800°C.
The optimal aging time and temperature needed to preserve nanoscale precipitates without over-aging are uncertain.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as an already homogeneous solid solution, while the first treatment step is said to homogenize it. The intended distinction between chemical homogenization, phase solutionizing, and the stated initial homogeneity is not resolved.
